key_insight: Metriplectic fluid models introduce irreversible dynamics while conserving energy, recovering energy-constrained Navier–Stokes in 2D and yielding new alternatives in 3D.
engineering_relevance: These models offer a framework for energy-preserving fluid simulation with selective dissipation of quantities such as potential enstrophy or helicity.
method: Augment Hamiltonian fluid dynamics with a symmetric, metric-based dissipative bracket.
Use Casimir invariants as generalized entropies driven monotonically while conserving energy.
Derive scalar-coupled anisotropic diffusion and helicity-driven dynamics on compact Riemannian manifolds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical model derivations and characterization of stationary states, but no numerical benchmarks or experimental validation.
watch_item: The helicity-driven term is non-smoothing, so monotonic entropy evolution should not be assumed to provide numerical regularization.
paper_title: Irreversible dynamics for ideal fluids on Riemannian manifolds: metriplectic energy-conserving alternatives to Navier-Stokes
